sections.what_happened: UPDATE: the Sunday Fox quotes from 2200-01 ('Do I make a deal with them, or do I finish them off? That's the only question.' / 'Remember, we now control the Hormuz Strait. They get nothing. Yes, we get everything.' / commercial activity above pre-war levels) are now carried by Times of Israel, TRT World, Dawn and L'Orient Today, plus WION (no registry tier, attribution only). NEW TO SCANS: asked whether a strike could come as soon as Sunday as he left the White House for a Michigan rally, Trump said: 'Would I tell you that? But the answer is no. There will not be a strike.' (Dawn 22:26+05 = 21:26 ; ANews 20:39+03 = 21:39 ; WION 23:42+05:30 = 22:12 , in-window.) The Taiwan 'stole our chip business, 100%' line was already inside 2200-01 and is not a new item. Fox News itself has no declared tier in the registry and is not counted; the 4 counted families are secondary reports of the same interview, so the QUOTES are now multi-family confirmed while the underlying Hormuz-control/commerce claims remain Trump's own claims only.
sections.what_verified: Quotes: 4 distinct declared-tier publisher families carry the same Fox interview wording (Times of Israel, TRT World, Dawn, L'Orient Today); WION also carries them but has no registry tier and does not count. Underlying Hormuz-control and above-pre-war-commerce claims: NO independent corroboration; contradicted in direction by counted PortWatch data (stale). The 2200-01 HOLD reason (single family) is now resolved for the quotes.
sections.what_disputed: IMF PortWatch (stale snapshot 2026-10-24, observation date 2026-10-18): counted 4 transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18, 7-day average 3.71/day vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day (4.3% of baseline) -- this contradicts 'commercial activity above pre-war levels' and does not measure 'control'. PortWatch count is STALE (6 days lag at fetch) and must be cited with its observation date, never as a live figure. No fresh PortWatch snapshot exists in ~/workspace/karim/news-scans/portwatch/ (newest is 2026-10-24).
sections.why_matters: Trump's Sunday fork in his own words -- deal or 'finish them off' -- now multi-sourced, plus his same-day denial that a strike comes Sunday; the counted number that undercuts his Hormuz claim: 4 transits on Oct 18 against a 2025 baseline of 85.5 a day (stale count, flagged as such).
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261025-2200-01 (gate flip) -- Trump Sunday Fox interview now carried by 4 declared-tier families, plus his separate no-strike-Sunday denial; Hormuz-control claim still contested by stale counted data

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump's Sunday fork in his own words -- deal or 'finish them off' -- now multi-sourced, plus his same-day denial that a strike comes Sunday; the counted number that undercuts his Hormuz claim: 4 transits on Oct 18 against a 2025 baseline of 85.5 a day (stale count, flagged as such). The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deal or finish-off: is Trump's Hormuz 'control' claim a negotiating bluff, or the prelude to a strike -- and do counted transits (near zero) prove the blockade, not commerce, is what the US actually controls? The no-strike-Sunday denial sharpens the fork: threat today, denial today.
